title: Microsoft Purview: Microsoft Graph APIs for archive mailboxes as EWS retires
notes: claim 67: severity major on a rationale: risk rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly says EWS disablement starts this month, although this November briefing's sources say October. It also treats licensing as wholly unpublished despite documented archive-service entitlements, and makes an unverified assurance that the EWS setting cannot restrict the Graph archive APIs.

claims.claim: Microsoft is adding Graph access to main and auxiliary archive mailboxes.
claims.quote: Access to Archive mailboxes (Main + Auxiliary) through Microsoft Graph.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a single seamless archive view across multiple auxiliary mailboxes.
claims.quote: The goal is to give users a single, seamless Archive view, even though Archive data may physically reside across multiple auxiliary mailboxes

claims.claim: MC1469565 says Graph now supports importing and exporting archive mailbox data.
claims.quote: Microsoft Graph now provides API support for importing and exporting mailbox data and for managing archive mailbox folders, including support for auto-expanding archives.

claims.claim: MC1469565 says Graph supports archive folder management, including auto-expanding archives.
claims.quote: Microsoft Graph now provides API support for importing and exporting mailbox data and for managing archive mailbox folders, including support for auto-expanding archives.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving creates auxiliary archive mailboxes.
claims.quote: An archive mailbox can include a main archive mailbox and one or more auxiliary archive mailboxes (created through autoexpanding archive).

claims.claim: A folder can appear in the main archive while its contents reside in an auxiliary archive.
claims.quote: In some cases, a folder appears in the main archive mailbox, but its contents actually reside in an auxiliary archive mailbox.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Accessing an expanded archive folder can return HTTP 308 and require a request to the redirect URL.
claims.quote: If the target resides in an auxiliary archive, the API returns a redirect response (such as `HTTP 308 Permanent Redirect`) with a redirect URL.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Archive export can return ErrorArchiveFolderMovedPermanently and require reissuing the request to the supplied URL.
claims.quote: For the item that returned `ErrorArchiveFolderMovedPermanently`, make a new POST request to the URL in the error message with the item ID to export it.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Importing an item into an auxiliary archive folder can return HTTP 409 identifying the target mailbox.
claims.quote: When you attempt to import an item into a folder that physically resides in an auxiliary (autoexpanded) archive mailbox, you receive an `HTTP 409 Conflict` response that indicates the correct target mailbox.

claims.claim: Resolving the auxiliary-archive import error requires a new import session for the indicated mailbox and a retry.
claims.quote: To resolve this issue, create a new import session targeting the mailbox ID indicated in the error message

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Archive folders must be referenced by folder ID because well-known folder names are unsupported.
claims.quote: Well-known folder names aren't supported for archive mailboxes. Reference folders in archive mailboxes by folder ID rather than by well-known folder name.
